Subject: Recap + next steps: POC/trial environment options (hosted vs sandbox vs VPC)

Alex — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned heading into the POC: 

Summary of call
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for Acme AI’s chat summarization workload (90% of queries under 512 tokens; 5k qps target for peak simulated load).
- Primary success criteria: 1) matching summary F1 >= 0.88 vs baseline, 2) median latency < 120ms for 95th percentile under target concurrency, 3) predictable cost estimate for monthly run-rate.

POC environment options we discussed
1) Hosted trial (fastest): Redwood-hosted API with isolated project. No infra setup required from Acme; ideal for functional verification and initial latency/cost profiling.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved pool): Dedicated GPU pool in our cloud that mimics production capacity — good for scale/load testing and throughput SLOs. Requires brief network allow-listing but minimal networking on your side.
3) VPC/private deployment (longer lead): Customer VPC peered to Redwood control plane or on-prem package — needed if you require customer-managed networking or stricter data residency. Has longer lead time (typically 2–4 weeks depending on approvals).

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
- You confirm which environment you want to start with (hosted or dedicated sandbox) — if you need VPC we'll start network prep and security questionnaire now.
- Acme to share sample prompt set + 2000 representative documents for quality tests (S3 link or Drive).
- Redwood (Vivek/Rishi) to send network and IAM checklist + test plan by EOD Monday.
- Target POC start date: Nov 30. If that works, we’ll schedule a kick-off and load test window.

Attachments: acme_poc_mop_v1.pdf (MOP draft), network_requirements.xlsx (network checklist stub)

Thanks — I’ll wait on your preference for environment and any adjustments to success criteria.

—
Marissa Cole

Alex/Priya — quick technical follow-up and checklist for Hosted trial so you can review with your infra team: 

Hosted trial (what to expect)- No VPC peering required. We provision an isolated project on our hosted control plane and provide API keys scoped to the trial. Data is stored encrypted at rest in our environment; if you need sample retention changes we can toggle retention windows.

Minimal access required from Acme- Allowlist Redwood outbound IPs for webhook callbacks (if you plan to use webhooks).- Provide S3 read-only link or Drive folder for sample data.- Provide list of IPs or CIDRs for any egress ACLs you control for test runners.

Network/IAM checklist (attached spreadsheet)
- API key generation & rotation guidance
- CORS / firewall notes for internal dashboard access
- Monitoring endpoints we will call during load tests

Load testing plan (high level)
- Day 1: Baseline functional tests with your labeled set (measure F1/hallucination).
- Day 2: Steady-state at 1k qps for 60m to measure median & 95pct latency and cost.
- Day 2 (later): 15m stress window ramping to 5k qps to validate autoscale/fallback behaviors.

Measuring quality
- We’ll run evaluation harness (we provide script) that computes summary F1 and a hallucination score (binary flag per item). We’ll share per-item results and aggregate metrics.

If you end up needing Dedicated sandbox instead, we’ll coordinate a short network allow-listing exercise and schedule dedicated GPU capacity — that usually adds 48–72 hours lead time versus Hosted. VPC/on-prem will need security review + KMS details and typically 2–4 weeks to stand up.

I’ll upload the test harness scripts and an example load configuration to the Drive link in the thread. Expect the checklist in the next message.
